title: Alphen aan den Rijn sword blade inscription (Archeon)

documents.route: unknown (inlaid on both faces of a medieval sword blade from Alphen aan den Rijn)

plaintext.source: No accepted reading; van Hasselt 2012 reads BENEDOXO as Benedicto Christo and MTINIUSCS as Martinius Sanctus, rest unexplained.

transcription.source: van Hasselt, Madoc 28/2 (2014) afb. 1 drawing from photographs; checked against Madoc and Wagner 2013 photographs
transcription.notes: Corroded inlay; photographs viewed, not reproduced. The sign printed as 7 is read Z.

system.summary: Two faces of capital letters inlaid on a sword blade; Latin-like benediction formula with a repeated group MTINIUSCSD; system unknown, no cipher shown.
system.notes: Vowels 32% (face A) and 41% (face B), so not an initials-only string; repeat MTINIUSCSD across faces.

prior_solution.where: van Hasselt 2014 (BENED, SCS, MTINIUS as Martinius); Wagner et al. 2009 and 2013 read the sibling family (SCS D X = Sanctus Dominus Christus); nobody has read Alphen as a whole.

conditions.human_role: Set the goal "solve the cipher behind the Alphen aan den Rijn Sword Inscription"; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: van Hasselt, van Halteren, Peters on the Alphen blade: partial Latin expansions, rest unread; transcriptions differ.
Vowels 12/38 face A, 17/41 face B; repeat MTINIUSCSD across faces; DIO x2, DIC x3.
Checked for a substitution: none indicated; text is Latin-like invocation with abbreviations and garbled letters. No expansion of the remainder is testable.
lm.best_language on both faces: Latin ranks first (-4.06/char) but only narrowly over French; no sign of substitution.
Found the Madoc 2014 article (Archeon PDF) with photographs and a transcription drawn from them, and Wagner et al. 2009 / Wagner 2013 on Uppsala DiVA.
Took van Hasselt's drawing as the text (replacing forum transcriptions); checked against the published photographs.
Aligned both faces to the Wagner/Worley readings of siblings: ISSCSD shared with Fyris 74, OXMTINIUS with W 1830, BENED with the Finnish sword.

Segmented both faces with the SDX-family expansions (SCS D = Sanctus Dominus, X = Christus, IS = Iesus, MTINIUS = Martinius): 56 of 79 (71%) letters fall in formula elements; the rest unexplained and the expansions are the sibling authors' tentative ones.

Longest common subsequence against shuffles of each face (3000): with Fyris 74 20/38 (A) p 0.033, 20/41 (B) p 0.026; with Marburg 14/38 p 0.008, 12/41 p 0.017; about 0.03-0.13 after Bonferroni over 2 references x 2 faces. Consistent with the SDX family, weaker than Witham. Two hypotheses, not checkable on the published images: the printed 7 is the Tironian et-sign, and face A ends in DNI = domini (witham1250/dudout/README.md).

outcome.method_basis: No key exists: the text is an invocation in abbreviations. A family-level parse (56 of 79 (71%) letters in formula elements, using sibling authors' expansions) is not a decipherment; the rest has no accepted expansion.
outcome.notes: Formula-level parse from the SDX family; remaining groups need the conservation report and an agreed expansion of the formulae.

credits.note: the transcription in inscription.txt (drawing from the photographs)
